C1-tu-youyou/01.claim: A Nobel Prize was hiding in a 1,600-year-old first-aid book.
C1-tu-youyou/01.sub: The clue was one boring detail.

C1-tu-youyou/02.definition: For fevers: soak a handful of qinghao (sweet wormwood) in water, wring out the juice, drink it.

C1-tu-youyou/03.definition: Her team was hunting a malaria drug. Their hot extracts kept failing. Then she noticed the recipe never said boil.

C1-tu-youyou/04.definition: Heat was destroying the active compound. Low-temperature extraction worked. The result was artemisinin, now a frontline malaria drug.

C1-tu-youyou/05.definition: Tu Youyou won the Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine. The footnote that mattered was 1,600 years old.

C1-tu-youyou/06.line: Somebody wrote it down. Somebody read it twice.
C1-tu-youyou/06.action: Modern artemisinin is purified and dosed. Wormwood juice is not a malaria treatment. History, not medical advice.

C2-confucius-not-yet/01.claim: A student told Confucius he’d mastered kindness.
C2-confucius-not-yet/01.sub: Confucius’s review was brutal. And weirdly hopeful.

C2-confucius-not-yet/02.quote: What I do not wish men to do to me, I also wish not to do to men.
C2-confucius-not-yet/02.note: Tsze-kung, his student, feeling pretty good about himself.

C2-confucius-not-yet/03.quote: Ts’ze, you have not attained to that.

C2-confucius-not-yet/04.definition: He didn’t say the idea was wrong. He said living it is harder than saying it. The most hopeful put-down in history.

C2-confucius-not-yet/05.definition: Do one thing for someone that you’d want done for you. Don’t announce it. That’s the gap between saying it and doing it.

C2-confucius-not-yet/06.line: Nobody’s there yet. That’s the fun part.
C2-confucius-not-yet/06.action: Tag the friend who says “I’m basically a saint.”

C3-goat-first/01.claim: Medieval Seville’s best doctor tested surgery on a goat first.

C3-goat-first/02.definition: Before anyone tried a tracheotomy on a person, he performed one on a goat to show it could be done safely.

C3-goat-first/03.definition: Wrote a thirty-volume medical encyclopedia and drew the surgical tools he used, probably the first drawings of their kind.

C3-goat-first/04.definition: A botanist who listed about 1,400 simple medicines from plants, animals and minerals.

C3-goat-first/05.term: Test it. Draw it. Write it down.
C3-goat-first/05.definition: Three habits that sound a lot like modern science. Al-Andalus had them a thousand years ago.

C3-goat-first/06.line: Curiosity, plus one very patient goat.
C3-goat-first/06.action: History, not medical advice. Some traditional remedies are toxic.

C4-always-pays/01.claim: The friend who always pays might be the happiest one at the table.
C4-always-pays/01.sub: There’s data on this. Sort of.

C4-always-pays/02.definition: People who had spent money on others in the past month reported more wellbeing in 120 of 136 countries. Linked, not proven to cause it.
C4-always-pays/02.cite: Aknin et al., J Pers Soc Psychol, 2013

C4-always-pays/03.definition: In a study of 46 people, those told to spend money on someone else ended the day happier than those who spent it on themselves. Later studies found smaller effects.

C4-always-pays/04.definition: Buy the coffee. Don’t mention it. Notice how the rest of the day feels.

C4-always-pays/05.line: Generous isn’t a personality. It’s a habit you can start on Monday.
C4-always-pays/05.action: Tag the friend who always pays. It’s your round.

C5-cheering-up-list/01.claim: Bad mood? An emperor’s fix: think about other people.
C5-cheering-up-list/01.sub: Not their faults. Their best bits.

C5-cheering-up-list/02.quote: When thou wishest to delight thyself, think of the virtues of those who live with thee; for instance, the activity of one, and the modesty of another, and the liberality of a third
C5-cheering-up-list/02.note: Marcus Aurelius, in his private notes.

C5-cheering-up-list/03.definition: A bad mood goes looking for what’s wrong, including in people. Marcus sends it looking for what’s right instead. (Moodius’s reading.)

C5-cheering-up-list/04.title: Pick four people
C5-cheering-up-list/04.body: Someone you live with, work with, text, or haven’t seen in years.

C5-cheering-up-list/05.title: One good quality each
C5-cheering-up-list/05.body: The one who’s always on time. The one who’s funny at funerals.

C5-cheering-up-list/06.title: Tell one of them
C5-cheering-up-list/06.body: A short message. No reason needed. Watch their day change. Then yours.

C5-cheering-up-list/07.line: The quickest mood lift is noticing someone.
C5-cheering-up-list/07.action: Tag the person you’d list first.

C6-timbuktu-tree/01.claim: A medical book in Timbuktu names a tree nobody can find.
C6-timbuktu-tree/01.sub: The knowledge survived. The plant went missing.

C6-timbuktu-tree/02.definition: Timbuktu scholars wrote down diagnoses and remedies using plants, animals and minerals, alongside prayers.

C6-timbuktu-tree/03.definition: Entries name local trees in Bambara and other local languages. Some, like a tree called Ṣukuru, scholars still can’t identify.

C6-timbuktu-tree/04.definition: Kept in at least 408 private family libraries in Mali.

C6-timbuktu-tree/05.line: Somewhere, a tree has a reputation it doesn’t know about.
C6-timbuktu-tree/05.action: History, not medical advice. Some traditional remedies are toxic.

stories/S1a-quiz-cold-water.label: Quick quiz
lines: A Nobel Prize came out of a 4th-century recipe.
Everyone else missed one detail in it. What was it?
Reply with your guess. Answer tomorrow at 9.

stories/S1b-answer-cold-water.label: Answer
lines: The old recipe never said boil. Heat was destroying the medicine. Full story at 12:00.
Tu Youyou, Nature Medicine, 2011. History, not medical advice.

stories/S2a-quiz-goat.label: Quick quiz
lines: Seville, 1100s. A doctor wants to try a new throat surgery.
Who did he test it on first?
Reply with your guess. Answer tomorrow at 9.

stories/S2b-answer-goat.label: Answer
lines: Ibn Zuhr proved the operation was safe before trying it on people. Full story at 12:00.
Karamanou et al., JBUON, 2015. History, not medical advice.
